maya: heads-up — seeing nondeterministic eval outputs on the quantized bring-up runs. same seed, same prompt, different tokens between CI and my laptop.
liam: ugh. which model and params?
maya: gptq-v1 on our qa-quant image. seed=42, top_p=0.9, temp=0.7. discrepancy shows up ~token 15 onwards.
liam: do you have a minimal repro command?
maya: yeah: ```python -m eval_runner --model gptq-v1 --seed 42 --top_p 0.9 --temp 0.7 --batch 1 --shard 0``` CI run uses `--shards 8` with worker reuse.
sasha: we merged the worker-reuse patch last week — might be related. worker process lifecycle changed (now warm-restarts instead of fresh forks).
maya: suspecting RNG lifecycle: master sets seed at test start, but worker warm-restart path calls `init_worker()` that calls `torch.manual_seed(os.getpid())` for some leftover debug code.
omar: whoa, that would definitely introduce nondet. can you grep for any `manual_seed` or `random.seed` in runner code?
maya: found one in `runner/worker_pool.py` — apparently added to avoid identical batches on startup. snippet:
```
# runner/worker_pool.py
def init_worker():
    import os
    import torch
    torch.manual_seed(os.getpid())
```
liam: that's a bug — seed should come from master or a deterministic function of the provided seed, not pid.
sasha: also check for numpy/python random usage in the sampler path. we mix `random`, `numpy.random`, and `torch` RNGs.
maya: confirmed: sampler uses `numpy.random.choice` for top_p bucketing. numpy isn't seeded in worker_init.
evalbot: flagged: possible causes = [worker-reseed-by-pid, mixed-RNG-not-seeded, cuda-init-after-fork]
omar: another angle — quantized kernels we load perform early CUDA init which can change CUDA RNG state if called after fork. If worker warm-restart triggers model load at a different time, that'd change sequence.
liam: so we have three suspects: 1) rogue pid-seed, 2) missing numpy/python seeds, 3) cuda init ordering + quant kernels.
sasha: short-term mitigation: remove pid-based seeding and add a worker_start hook that sets all RNGs from the experiment seed. e.g.:
```
def worker_start(seed):
    import random, numpy as np, torch
    random.seed(seed)
    np.random.seed(seed)
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)
```
But we need to ensure this happens before model load / CUDA init.
maya: I'll prototype ordering: set seeds immediately after fork and before importing model backends. That should prevent cuda-init-from-model from shifting RNG.
omar: CI change: add a small job that runs 3 seeds on quantized model with `--force-restart-workers` and also with `--warm-reuse` to compare. If outputs match when we restart workers but diverge when reusing, we've nailed it.
liam: long-term: add deterministic sampler that uses a single RNG source (torch.Generator) and avoid numpy/python in hot path; or at least wire them to the same seed via `torch.Generator`'s integer stream.
sasha: caution: `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)` may break quant kernels; tests should guard for that.
maya: opened draft PR with the pid-seed removal + worker_start hook, plus a tiny regression test that runs 2 seeds and diffs outputs. posting link in a sec. :thumbsup:
liam: nice. also add dashboard metric: per-run token-level hash and a flakiness flag if same-seed runs disagree — that'll help catch regressions in model onboarding.
evalbot: note: if nondet persists after fixes, collect `strace` + `LD_PRELOAD=libasan` runs to check for uninitialized reads in C kernels.
sasha: agreed. thanks for triaging — assigning to me and maya to follow up. will add CI job and open a follow-up to move sampler to torch.Generator.
maya: thanks folks. I'll attach the raw CI logs and the small binary diff I grabbed between seeds.
liam: rough plan timeline: hotfix to remove pid-seed today, CI job + test by tomorrow, sampler refactor as follow-up. if anyone needs help ping me.
maya: noted. ending thread with reproduced minimal steps in gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/repro-quant-seed (will update)
